title: Waiting six weeks for the fourteenth man and playing Trees at Hartford
summary: Because of Ellington's superstition about thirteen men Brown waited unpaid until Otto Hardwick joined, then debuted at the Colonial Theater in Hartford.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So what was your first date with the band? Where was the first place you played?

When I came from the Coast, we went to Hartford, Connecticut, where we rehearsed. I didn't play with the band up there. I didn't play with the band at first, because I was the 13th man. And there was so much -- what you call it -- superstition, that oh, no, not 13 men. Had to wait for the 14th man.

And the 14th man was Otto Hardwick, and at that time he was working some where in Washington, doing something, and he couldn't come until later. So my first actual date of playing was at the theater, I think it was the Colonial Theater in Hartford, Connecticut. And of all numbers, I was playing this solo tune, 'Trees'. Scared to death, again.

No, just me. I -- they framed up a whole concerto-like thing, see, and naturally after playing with Louie Armstrong so long, and being so crazy about him, I sort of ended in a Louis Armstrong type ending. You know, long, strung out thing. And that was the first number.
So how long had you been with the band then, and not playing with it? How long had you been hired before you played there in Connecticut?
I was with the band. I wasn't hired until I played my first job.
You didn't get paid all this time?
No. It was about six weeks.
Yeah, it was about six weeks.
Was everybody this concerned about there being 13, or was it just Duke?
No, it was just Duke, as far as the rest of them, it didn't make any difference.
But Duke wouldn't have had the 13 --
Oh, he's very superstitious. Very superstitious.
